konu: Basic body parts and physical features; clothes; daily routines and activities
ciktilar: ENG.5.3.L1-L4. Students can understand and bring together significant details about basic body parts, physical features, clothes, and daily routines while listening/watching.

ENG.5.3.G1 & V1. Students can select and use target vocabulary (body parts, adjectives, clothes, accessories, routine verbs) and grammatical structures (have/has got, comparatives, Simple Present, possessive adjectives, question tags).
ENG.5.3.P1, S1 & W1. Students can pronounce plural/third-person -s endings accurately and describe people's physical features, clothing habits, and daily routines in speaking and writing.
giris: In Week 14 of «Theme 3: Personal Life», we bring together all three sub-themes of our unit: «Basic body parts and physical features; clothes; daily routines and activities». We learn how to name parts of the human body, describe what people look like using «to be» and «have got / has got», compare physical features and clothes using comparative adjectives, and talk about what we wear and what we do every day using the Simple Present Tense, frequency adverbs, and question tags.

bolumler.baslik: Basic Body Parts and Physical Features Vocabulary
metin: To describe a person accurately in English, we first need to know the target nouns for basic body parts: {koyu:a head} (baş), {koyu:a face} (yüz), {koyu:hair} (saç), {koyu:an eye} (göz), {koyu:a nose} (burun), {koyu:a neck} (boyun), {koyu:an arm} (kol), {koyu:a hand} (el), {koyu:a finger} (el parmağı), {koyu:a leg} (bacak), {koyu:a foot} (ayak), {koyu:a tooth} (diş), {koyu:a body} (vücut) and {koyu:height} (boy uzunluğu). Most body parts form their plural by adding «-s» ({koyu:two eyes, two arms, ten fingers, two legs}), whereas {koyu:tooth} becomes {koyu:teeth} (dişler) and {koyu:foot} becomes {koyu:feet} (ayaklar). In addition, {koyu:hair} is used as an uncountable singular noun in English (e.g., «Her hair is long»).

We combine these nouns with descriptive adjectives for physical features. For height and body build, we use {koyu:tall} (uzun boylu), {koyu:short} (kısa boylu), {koyu:thin} (zayıf/ince) and {koyu:average} (orta boylu/yapılı). For hair style and length, we use {koyu:straight} (düz), {koyu:wavy} (dalgalı), {koyu:curly} (kıvırcık), {koyu:long} (uzun) and {koyu:short} (kısa). For face shapes, we use {koyu:round} (yuvarlak), {koyu:oval} (oval) and {koyu:square} (kare).

kutular.metin: One tooth - thirty-two teeth (diş - dişler); one foot - two feet (ayak - ayaklar). «Hair» (saç) tekil kabul edilir, «a hair» veya «hairs» denmez: «She has got wavy hair.»
Saç şekilleri: straight (düz), wavy (dalgalı), curly (kıvırcık). Yüz şekilleri: round (yuvarlak), oval (oval), square (kare).

satirlar: head, face, eye, nose, tooth / teeth, hair
baş, yüz, göz, burun, diş/dişler, saç

liste: «An eye» and «an arm» take «an» because they start with a vowel sound.
When multiple adjectives describe hair, length comes before style and colour: «long straight black hair».

bolumler.baslik: Describing Physical Appearance: To Be vs. Have Got and Has Got
metin: When we ask about someone's physical appearance, we use the question «{koyu:What does he / she look like?}» (O nasıl görünür? / Fiziksel görünüşü nasıldır?). Do not confuse this with «What is he/she like?» which asks about personality. When answering, we use two different verb structures depending on whether we use an adjective alone or a noun phrase.

We use {koyu:am / is / are} before height and build adjectives: «I {koyu:am} tall and thin», «He {koyu:is} of average height», «They {koyu:are} short». On the other hand, we use {koyu:have got} (with I, you, we, they) and {koyu:has got} (with he, she, it) when describing specific body parts such as eyes, hair, face, or nose: «She {koyu:has got} curly brown hair and green eyes», «He {koyu:has got} a round face and a small nose».

«What does Kerem look like?» — «He is tall and thin. He has got short straight hair and brown eyes.»

satirlar: We are tall and average build.

Kare bir yüzü ve kısa saçı var.

liste: Negative forms: «I haven't got curly hair» / «She hasn't got blue eyes».
Question forms: «Have you got long hair? — Yes, I have.» / «Has he got glasses? — No, he hasn't.»

bolumler.baslik: Clothes, Accessories and Seasonal Clothing Habits
metin: Our personal life also includes the clothes and accessories we wear in different seasons and occasions. For everyday clothing, our target vocabulary includes {koyu:a T-shirt} (tişört), {koyu:a shirt} (gömlek), {koyu:a jumper / a sweater} (kazak), {koyu:a jacket} (ceket), {koyu:a coat} (kaban/mont), {koyu:a raincoat} (yağmurluk), {koyu:a dress} (elbise), {koyu:a skirt} (etek), {koyu:trousers / pants} (pantolon), {koyu:jeans} (kot pantolon), {koyu:shorts} (şort), {koyu:socks} (çoraplar), {koyu:shoes} (ayakkabılar), {koyu:boots} (bot/çizme) and {koyu:a (fancy dress) costume} (kostüm).

We complete our outfits with accessories and jewellery: {koyu:a belt} (kemer), {koyu:a hat} (şapka), {koyu:a cap} (kasketli şapka), {koyu:a scarf} (atkı/fular), {koyu:a headscarf} (başörtüsü), {koyu:gloves} (eldiven), {koyu:glasses} (gözlük), {koyu:sunglasses} (güneş gözlüğü), {koyu:a bag / a handbag} (çanta / el çantası), {koyu:an umbrella} (şemsiye), {koyu:a watch} (kol saati), {koyu:a ring} (yüzük), {koyu:a necklace} (kolye), {koyu:earrings} (küpe) and {koyu:silver} (gümüş) items. Notice that words with two parts like {koyu:trousers, jeans, shorts, glasses, sunglasses, shoes, boots, gloves, socks, earrings} are plural and take «are» (e.g., «My jeans are blue»).

Trousers, jeans, shorts, glasses, sunglasses, shoes, boots, socks, gloves ve earrings çoğul kullanılır; tek bir tanesini belirtmek için «a pair of jeans / shoes» denir.

satirlar: fancy dress costume, stylish shirt, dress

liste: We use «wear» for both clothes and accessories: «She wears a headscarf, a coat, and a silver ring.»
We use «carry» or «take» with an umbrella or a handbag: «Take your umbrella; it is rainy today.»

metin: To state who owns an item of clothing or whose body part we are describing, we use {koyu:possessive adjectives} before nouns: {koyu:my} (benim), {koyu:your} (senin/sizin), {koyu:his} (onun - erkek), {koyu:her} (onun - kız), {koyu:its} (onun - cansız/hayvan), {koyu:our} (bizim), and {koyu:their} (onların). For example: «{koyu:His} jacket is black, and {koyu:her} handbag is brown.»

When we compare the physical features or clothes of two people, we use {koyu:comparative adjectives} followed by {koyu:than}. One-syllable adjectives take «-er»: {koyu:tall - taller than}, {koyu:short - shorter than}, {koyu:long - longer than}. Adjectives ending in consonant-vowel-consonant double the last letter: {koyu:thin - thinner than}, {koyu:big - bigger than}. Adjectives ending in «-y» change to «-ier»: {koyu:curly - curlier than}. Long adjectives with two or more syllables take «more»: {koyu:more comfortable than}, {koyu:more colourful than}. Irregular adjectives change completely: {koyu:good - better than}, {koyu:bad - worse than}.

satirlar: Burak is taller than his brother.
A T-shirt is thinner than a winter coat.
Selin's hair is curlier than my hair.
Trainers are more comfortable than boots.
A raincoat is better than a jumper in the rain.

liste: Always use «than» when both compared items are in the sentence: «My bag is heavier than your bag.»
Possessive adjectives must be followed by a noun: «my shoes, your watch, our classroom, their costumes».

bolumler.baslik: Daily Routines, Activities, Time Expressions and Frequency Adverbs
metin: To talk about our daily routines and free-time activities, we use the {koyu:Simple Present Tense}. With {koyu:I, you, we, they}, we use the base form of the verb ({koyu:wake up, wash, brush, get dressed, have, go, do, sleep}). With third-person singular subjects ({koyu:he, she, it}), we add {koyu:-s, -es, or -ies} to the verb in affirmative sentences ({koyu:wakes up, washes, brushes, gets dressed, has breakfast, goes to school, does homework, studies}). In negative and question sentences, we use {koyu:don't / doesn't} and {koyu:Do / Does} with the base verb.

We express how often we do an activity with {koyu:frequency adverbs}: {koyu:always} (%100 - her zaman), {koyu:usually} (%80 - genellikle), {koyu:often} (%60 - sık sık), {koyu:sometimes} (%40 - bazen), and {koyu:never} (%0 - asla). They go before main verbs («She {koyu:always brushes} her teeth») but after am/is/are («He {koyu:is never} late»). For time expressions, we use {koyu:at} with clock times and night ({koyu:at 7 o'clock, at half past seven, at quarter to eight, at night}), {koyu:in} with parts of the day and seasons ({koyu:in the morning, in winter}), and {koyu:on} with days ({koyu:on Mondays, on Sunday morning}).

  <text x="520" y="168" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#831843">(in the morning, in the afternoon, in winter)</text>
  <text x="520" y="194" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#831843">• ON + Günler (on Monday, on Fridays)</text>
  <text x="520" y="218" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#9d174d">How often do you...? / What time does she...?</text>
</svg>

kutular.metin: He/She/It öznelerinde: have -> has (She has breakfast); go -> goes; wash -> washes; brush -> brushes; watch -> watches; study -> studies.
«Never» cümleye olumsuz anlam katar ancak olumlu cümle yapısıyla kullanılır; «doesn't never» denmez: «He never wears a hat.»

satirlar: Clock times, noon, night, the weekend
She wakes up at quarter past seven (07:15).
Parts of the day, months, seasons
I do my homework in the afternoon.
Days of the week, specific dates
We have sports club on Wednesdays.
I usually wear a jumper in autumn.

liste: Telling the time: 07:00 = seven o'clock · 07:15 = quarter past seven · 07:30 = half past seven · 07:45 = quarter to eight.
In questions with «Does», the main verb loses its «-s»: «What time does he get dressed?»

bolumler.baslik: Question Tags and Pronunciation of Final -s / -es Sounds
metin: In everyday conversation, we use {koyu:question tags} («değil mi?») at the end of a statement to confirm information or ask for agreement. The golden rule is: {koyu:a positive statement takes a negative tag, and a negative statement takes a positive tag}. With «to be», we repeat the form of be: «She {koyu:is} tall, {koyu:isn't she}?», «Your boots {koyu:aren't} new, {koyu:are they}?». With Simple Present verbs, we use {koyu:don't / doesn't} or {koyu:do / does}: «You {koyu:wear} glasses, {koyu:don't you}?», «He {koyu:gets} up early, {koyu:doesn't he}?», «She {koyu:doesn't like} rings, {koyu:does she}?».

In pronunciation (ENG.5.3.P1), the final {koyu:-s / -es} in plural nouns (like clothes and body parts) and third-person singular verbs is pronounced in three different ways: 1) {koyu:/s/} after voiceless sounds (p, t, k, f): {koyu:caps, coats, boots, shirts, skirts, socks, walks, gets}. 2) {koyu:/z/} after vowels and voiced sounds (b, d, g, l, m, n, r, v): {koyu:shoes, jeans, gloves, bags, rings, eyes, legs, wears, goes}. 3) {koyu:/ız/} after sibilant sounds (s, sh, ch, x, z): {koyu:dresses, glasses, sunglasses, watches, necklaces, brushes, washes}.
bolumler.gorsel:

kutular.metin: Olumlu cümle + Olumsuz tag (+ , -?): «He has got brown eyes, hasn't he?» / «She wears a scarf, doesn't she?». Olumsuz cümle + Olumlu tag (- , +?).
Kelime -ss, -sh, -ch, -ce, -ge ile bitiyorsa -es eki ekstra bir hece olarak /ız/ okunur: dresses, glasses, watches, brushes, washes.

satirlar: caps, coats, boots, shirts, skirts, socks
shoes, jeans, gloves, bags, rings, eyes, arms

liste: Question tag subject must always be a pronoun (he, she, it, they), not a proper noun: «Ali is tall, isn't he?»
Practising /s/, /z/, and /ız/ sounds helps us speak clearly and understand listening tracks accurately.

ornekler.soru: «What does your best friend Elif look like?» sorusunu Elif'in uzun boylu, zayıf, uzun dalgalı kahverengi saçlı ve yeşil gözlü olduğunu belirterek İngilizce cevaplayınız.
ornekler.cevap: «She is tall and thin. She has got long wavy brown hair and green eyes.» (Boy ve yapı için «is», saç ve göz için «has got» kullanılır.)
ornekler.cozum: «She is tall and thin. She has got long wavy brown hair and green eyes.» (Boy ve yapı için «is», saç ve göz için «has got» kullanılır.)
ornekler.ipucu: Sıfatlardan önce «is», isim tamlamalarından (hair, eyes) önce «has got» kullanmayı unutmayınız.

ornekler.soru: «Soğuk ve yağmurlu bir kış gününde dışarı çıkarken ne giyersin ve yanına ne alırsın?» sorusuna hedef giysi ve aksesuar kelimelerinden en az dördünü kullanarak İngilizce bir cümle kurunuz.
ornekler.cevap: «On a cold and rainy day, I wear a raincoat, a warm jumper, boots, and gloves, and I take my umbrella.»
ornekler.cozum: «On a cold and rainy day, I wear a raincoat, a warm jumper, boots, and gloves, and I take my umbrella.»
ornekler.ipucu: Kış ve yağmur kelimeleri olan raincoat, coat, jumper, boots, scarf, gloves ve umbrella sözcüklerinden yararlanınız.

ornekler.soru: Verilen bilgileri karşılaştırma sıfatlarıyla (comparative adjectives) birleştiriniz: 1) Mert (158 cm) / Can (150 cm) [tall] — 2) Boots / Trainers [comfortable].
ornekler.cevap: 1) «Mert is taller than Can.» (Kısa sıfata -er eklenir.) — 2) «Trainers are more comfortable than boots.» (Uzun sıfata more eklenir.)
ornekler.cozum: 1) «Mert is taller than Can.» (Kısa sıfata -er eklenir.) — 2) «Trainers are more comfortable than boots.» (Uzun sıfata more eklenir.)
ornekler.ipucu: Tek heceli sıfatlara «-er than», çok heceli sıfatların önüne «more ... than» getirilir.

ornekler.soru: Aşağıdaki cümlelerde boş bırakılan yerlere uygun zaman edatlarını (at / in / on) ve fiil çekimlerini yerleştiriniz: «Beren usually ___ (wake up) ___ half past seven ___ the morning ___ weekdays.»
ornekler.cevap: «Beren usually wakes up at half past seven in the morning on weekdays.» (Beren tekil özne olduğu için wakes up; saatlerde at, günün bölümlerinde in, günlerde on kullanılır.)
ornekler.cozum: «Beren usually wakes up at half past seven in the morning on weekdays.» (Beren tekil özne olduğu için wakes up; saatlerde at, günün bölümlerinde in, günlerde on kullanılır.)
ornekler.ipucu: Saatler için «at», «the morning» için «in», günler için «on» edatını seçiniz.

ornekler.soru: Aşağıdaki cümlelerin sonuna uygun «question tag» (değil mi?) ifadelerini ekleyiniz: 1) «She wears glasses, ...?» — 2) «Your shoes aren't black, ...?»
ornekler.cevap: 1) «She wears glasses, doesn't she?» (Geniş zaman olumlu tekil cümle -> olumsuz tag: doesn't she?) — 2) «Your shoes aren't black, are they?» (Çoğul olumsuz to be cümlesi -> olumlu tag: are they?)
ornekler.cozum: 1) «She wears glasses, doesn't she?» (Geniş zaman olumlu tekil cümle -> olumsuz tag: doesn't she?) — 2) «Your shoes aren't black, are they?» (Çoğul olumsuz to be cümlesi -> olumlu tag: are they?)
ornekler.ipucu: Cümle olumluysa tag olumsuz, cümle olumsuzsa tag olumlu olur.

ornekler.soru: «coats, watches, gloves, shirts, dresses, shoes» kelimelerini sonlarındaki «-s / -es» ekinin okunuşuna (/s/, /z/, /ız/) göre üç gruba ayırınız.
ornekler.cevap: 1) /s/ sesiyle okunanlar: coats, shirts. — 2) /z/ sesiyle okunanlar: gloves, shoes. — 3) /ız/ sesiyle okunanlar: watches, dresses.
ornekler.cozum: 1) /s/ sesiyle okunanlar: coats, shirts. — 2) /z/ sesiyle okunanlar: gloves, shoes. — 3) /ız/ sesiyle okunanlar: watches, dresses.
ornekler.ipucu: -t ile bitenler /s/, ünlü veya -v ile bitenler /z/, -ch ve -ss ile bitenler /ız/ sesini verir.

etkinlikler.soru: Ayla: «What does your new classmate Demir look like?» — Bora: «_______________» Diyalogdaki boşluğa aşağıdakilerden hangisi getirilmelidir?
secenekler: He is tall and thin, and he has got short curly hair.
He usually goes to school by bus at eight o'clock.
He likes playing basketball and reading adventure books.
He has got a blue schoolbag and two notebooks on his desk.
etkinlikler.aciklama: «What does he look like?» sorusu kişinin boy, kilo, saç ve göz gibi dış görünüş özelliklerini sorar.

etkinlikler.soru: «It is very cold and snowy outside today. Put on your warm ________, ________, and ________ before you go out.» cümlesinde boşluklara anlamca en uygun düşen giysi grubu hangisidir?
etkinlikler.aciklama: Soğuk ve karlı havada kaban (coat), atkı (scarf) ve eldiven (gloves) giyilir.

etkinlikler.soru: «My sister Pelin ________ up at quarter past seven every morning, ________ her teeth, and gets dressed for school.» cümlesindeki boşluklara sırasıyla hangi fiiller gelmelidir?
etkinlikler.aciklama: Üçüncü tekil şahıs (My sister Pelin = She) ile geniş zamanda «wake» fiili «wakes», «-sh» ile biten «brush» fiili ise «brushes» olur.

etkinlikler.soru: «Zeynep has got wavy hair, ________? And she wears silver earrings, ________?» cümlelerindeki question tag boşluklarına sırasıyla hangileri getirilmelidir?
etkinlikler.aciklama: İlk cümlede «has got» olumlu olduğu için «hasn't she?», ikinci cümlede geniş zaman «wears» olumlu olduğu için «doesn't she?» kullanılır.

ifadeler.aciklama: Tooth (teeth) ve foot (feet) düzensiz çoğul vücut bölümleridir.
ifadeler.ifade: The plural form of «a tooth» is «teeth», and the plural form of «a foot» is «feet».

ifadeler.aciklama: Saç ve göz gibi isim tamlamalarıyla «is» değil, «has got» kullanılır: «She has got long curly hair and green eyes.»
ifadeler.ifade: To describe someone's hair and eyes, we say «She is long curly hair and green eyes».

ifadeler.aciklama: Ünsüz-ünlü-ünsüz ile biten tek heceli «thin» sıfatı karşılaştırma eki alırken «thinner» şeklinde yazılır.
ifadeler.ifade: In the sentence «My brother is thinner than me», the comparative form of «thin» is written with a double «n».

ifadeler.aciklama: Saatlerden önce «on» değil, «at» edatı kullanılır: «at half past seven».
ifadeler.ifade: We use the preposition «on» before clock times, such as «on half past seven».

ifadeler.aciklama: -ss ve -ch sesleriyle biten kelimeler çoğul olduğunda /ız/ sesiyle okunur.
ifadeler.ifade: The plural words «dresses, glasses, watches» end with the /ız/ pronunciation sound.

etkinlikler.soru: Aşağıdaki ifadeleri Doğru (D) veya Yanlış (Y) olarak değerlendiriniz.

ciftler: She is tall and has got wavy brown hair.
He is wearing a blue jumper, jeans, and boots.
What time does she wake up?
She wakes up at quarter past seven (07:15).
How often do you wear a cap?
I sometimes wear a cap on sunny days.
Your coat is warmer than mine, isn't it?
Yes, it is very thick and comfortable.
etkinlikler.soru: Aşağıdaki kavram ve açıklamaları doğru şekilde eşleştiriniz.

cumleler.metin: A person has got two feet and ten toes, and two hands and ten ___.
It is raining heavily outside; don't forget to wear your ___ and take your umbrella.
Emre is 165 cm and Kaan is 155 cm, so Emre is ___ than Kaan.
My sister is a boy's sister, so for a girl's necklace we use the possessive adjective ___.
We usually have breakfast ___ half past seven in the morning.

etkinlikler.soru: Aşağıdaki cümlelerde boş bırakılan yerleri uygun kavramlarla tamamlayınız.

Write a cohesive 4-sentence paragraph in English about your cousin Arda covering: 1) His height, build, hair, and eyes, 2) A comparison between Arda and you, 3) His favourite clothes and accessories, and 4) His morning routine with time.
ipuclari: 1. İpucu: İlk cümlede «He is ...» ile boy/kilo, «He has got ...» ile saç/göz ve yüz şeklini belirtiniz.
2. İpucu: İkinci cümlede «taller than» veya «younger than» gibi bir karşılaştırma yapısı kullanınız.
3. İpucu: Üçüncü ve dördüncü cümlelerde giydiği kıyafetleri (wears) ve sabah rutinini saat edatıyla (at ... in the morning) yazınız.
etkinlikler.cevap: 1) My cousin Arda is tall and thin, and he has got short straight black hair, brown eyes, and an oval face. 2) He is taller than me, but my hair is curlier than his hair. 3) He usually wears a blue jumper, jeans, trainers, and a silver watch at school. 4) Every weekday, he wakes up at seven o'clock in the morning, brushes his teeth, and has breakfast with his family.
etkinlikler.cozum: 1) My cousin Arda is tall and thin, and he has got short straight black hair, brown eyes, and an oval face. 2) He is taller than me, but my hair is curlier than his hair. 3) He usually wears a blue jumper, jeans, trainers, and a silver watch at school. 4) Every weekday, he wakes up at seven o'clock in the morning, brushes his teeth, and has breakfast with his family.

ozet: Basic body parts include head, face, eye, nose, neck, arm, hand, finger, leg, foot (plural: feet), tooth (plural: teeth), hair, body, and height.

Physical appearance is described with «am/is/are» for height and build (tall, short, thin, average) and «have got / has got» for hair (curly, wavy, straight), eyes, and face shape (round, oval, square).

Clothing and accessories vocabulary covers seasonal outfits (coat, raincoat, jumper/sweater, jacket, T-shirt, shirt, dress, skirt, trousers/pants, jeans, shorts, boots, shoes, scarf, gloves, umbrella, sunglasses, watch, ring, necklace, earrings).
Comparative adjectives (-er than / more ... than) compare two people or items, while possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, its, our, their) show ownership before nouns.
Daily routines use the Simple Present Tense with frequency adverbs (always, usually, often, sometimes, never), time prepositions (at/in/on), question tags, and accurate /s/, /z/, /ız/ pronunciation.
